thread.title: Apple ( AAPL ) saw its end to consistent iPhone sales growth

author: Damon Verial
title: Apple ( AAPL ) saw its end to consistent iPhone sales growth
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) saw its end to consistent iPhone sales growth in April 2016. Investors panicked, dropping the stock and creating a gap. I was there, not panicking but buying Apple - because I'm a gap trader, and when I ran the analyses, I was certain that this was a mere bump in a long road upward, a chart full of up breakaway gaps and down area gaps .
If the current drawdown in Apple were like that of April, I would be buying again, playing the gap. The difference this time, however, is that we don't have a gap upon which I can run the probability models, my gap algorithm, and other machine learning techniques. No, this is something I consider much more organic: A selloff before an earnings report.
I have already written about Apple's earnings forecast in my newsletter, recommending my subscribers take a long position. While a four-day-plus selloff before earnings is typically a bad omen for the EPS, guidance, or stock price on the earnings release date, it can also be overblown. Case-in-point: Apple, which just retraced a 20-day high to hit a 20-day low.
This in my experience is not indicative of a looming earnings selloff but of profit taking. Just as my data on insider trading shows that it can mean multiple things for the stock's future (namely: insider buying predicts rising prices, while selling predicts consolidation instead of the selloff you would expect), a selloff before earnings can have multiple implications, conditional on other recent factors. At a pace we are currently witnessing in Apple, a selloff typically indicates profit taking prior to a risky event and drives the price to one that discounts the stock on the assumption of poor earnings or guidance.
I have written before on the importance of earnings for Apple , and through watching Apple's earnings reactions quarter after quarter believe that investor movement around these days has changed in a significant fashion. Whereas before, investors were expecting to be blown away with explosive sales numbers, new product announcements, and ever-increasing optimism from management, today we have a very different Apple. Arguably, the Apple of today offers significantly less upside than that of yesterday, but that's a good thing!
